pronunciation.t: I fixed it or I’ll fix it?
pronunciation.tip: No I’ll, o som é “ÁIL”, com o L no fim, e o verbo fica sem -ed: fix. No fixed, o fim é um T rápido: “FIKST”.
thirTEEN: a força fica no fim, “thâr-TÍIN”. THIRty: a força fica no começo, “THÂR-di”.

dialogue.g: Ana, você tem um minuto? Tem um bug antes do lançamento. O botão “Buy now” não aparece no celular.
Nas telas pequenas. Quando o pop-up abre, ele cobre o botão. Eu testei em três celulares, e quebra em todos.
Hum. E se a gente mudar o botão para cima das fotos?
Boa ideia, mas o design vai mudar. Você pode conferir hoje? O lançamento é na sexta.
Claro. Eu te mando uma versão nova hoje à tarde. Você já falou com o Leo?
Ainda não. Eu escrevi para ele, mas ele ainda não respondeu. Ele está numa reunião.
Tá. E o leitor de tela? Semana passada, ele não lia o botão.
Isso eu já consertei. Agora ele lê “Buy now”. Eu testei ontem de olhos fechados!
Ha! Perfeito. Vamos consertar a versão do celular, e aí a gente pode publicar.

dialogueQuestions.q: What’s the problem with the button?
dialogueQuestions.a: It doesn’t show on small screens. When the pop-up opens, it covers the button.
To move the button above the pictures: “What if we move the button above the pictures?”
Not yet. She’s written to him, but he hasn’t answered yet.
The screen reader. Now it reads “Buy now”.

grammar: I’ve fixed the menu. I’ve tested it on three phones.
I’ve worked with React for two years. · I’ve worked here since 2024.
trabalho com React há dois anos · trabalho aqui desde 2024
I built a shop page last year. I fixed it yesterday.
fiz no ano passado · consertei ontem

listeningQuestions.q: Leo has looked at the new version on his computer.
Leo wants a bigger button on mobile.
Everything is ready for the launch. How do you know?
listeningQuestions.say: No. The button is too small, and the tests haven’t finished yet.

corrections.why: Desde 2023 até hoje: I’ve worked … since.
Com data (yesterday, last week), use o passado, sem I’ve.
O que ainda não aconteceu: haven’t … yet.

corrections.s: Could you to check the form?
corrections.why: Depois de could you, o verbo vem direto, sem to.
Realize é perceber. “Realizar os testes” é run the tests.

interview: Hi, thanks for joining! Can you hear me OK? Great. So, tell me a little about yourself.
What have you built? Tell me about a project you’re proud of.
Interesting! What was the hardest part?
A lot of our users are on their phones. How do you make a page work on mobile?
And how do you make a page accessible? For example, for people who use a screen reader.
Tell me about a bug you fixed. What happened, and how did you fix it?
In our team, we review each other’s code. How do you deal with feedback in a code review?
Great. That’s all from me. Do you have any questions for us?
steps: Answer Jun’s questions, with an example from your work.

Ask Jun two questions about the job.

Choose a project. Explain the problem, what you did and the result. Bring your example to the next class.

text.D.1: Ana, do you have a minute? There’s a bug before the launch. The “Buy now” button doesn’t show on mobile.
text.D.3: On small screens. When the pop-up opens, it covers the button. I’ve tested it on three phones, and it breaks on all of them.
text.D.4: Hmm. What if we move the button above the pictures?
text.D.5: Good idea, but the design will change. Could you check it today? The launch is on Friday.
text.D.6: Sure. I’ll send you a new version this afternoon. Have you talked to Leo?
text.D.7: Not yet. I’ve written to him, but he hasn’t answered yet. He’s in a meeting.
text.D.8: OK. And what about the screen reader? Last week, it didn’t read the button.
text.D.9: I’ve already fixed that. Now it reads “Buy now”. I tested it yesterday with my eyes closed!
text.D.10: Ha! Perfect. Let’s fix the mobile version, and then we can deploy.
